turns.prompt:
You are given two attached CSV files describing perovskite solar cells as
complete devices — `substrate` (glass + transparent electrode), `etl`
(electron-transport layer stack), `htl` (hole-transport layer stack),
`backcontact` (metal / carbon back electrode), `deposition` (absorber
deposition procedure; `>>` separates steps). Every candidate below uses the
same MAPbI3 absorber in the same p-i-n (inverted) architecture; they differ
only in the remaining columns. Each row is a device CONFIGURATION whose
efficiency is the median over at least 3 independently fabricated cells, so
it is a reproducible recipe rather than a single champion cell:
  - b3_pvk_stack_pin_train.csv: 300 configurations with the measured power
    conversion efficiency (%).
  - b3_pvk_stack_pin_pool.csv: 100 CANDIDATE configurations whose power
    conversion efficiency (%) was NOT measured, columns `candidate_id` and
    the same device columns.

Using the training data, select the 5 candidates with the HIGHEST power
conversion efficiency (%).

Reason from the device physics — band alignment and selectivity of the
transport layers, interface recombination, contact chemistry and the film
quality the process is likely to give — then end your answer with an
explicit ranked list of candidate_ids, best first, e.g. "Final: c901, c902,
c903, c904, c905".
turns.answer_text:
## Reasoning

**Key patterns in the training data driving the highest efficiencies (>17%):**

1. **ETL selectivity**: Fullerene-based ETLs with a dipole/blocking interlayer (C60 | BCP, PCBM-60 | BCP, or PCBM-60 | C60 | BCP) dominate the top of the distribution — BCP suppresses back-electron transfer and improves Voc/FF versus bare PCBM/C60.

2. **HTL selectivity**: Among HTLs, **PTAA** and **P3CT-Na** consistently outperform plain PEDOT:PSS in the top rows (14–19%), reflecting better energy-level alignment with MAPbI3 and lower interfacial trap density than acidic PEDOT:PSS. NiO-c with functionalized interlayers (Zr(acac)4, SDBS, PTAA capping) also reaches high efficiency.

3. **Back contact chemistry**: **Cu** contacts paired with PTAA give the very highest results in the training set (18.62%, 18.85%, 19.085%) — likely because Cu is compatible with the PTAA/fullerene stack and avoids Ag/PEDOT diffusion issues, while also reducing parasitic absorption/contact resistance losses seen with Al on PTAA.

4. Small molecular dye/interlayer modifiers at the ETL/perovskite interface (Rhodamine 101, ITCPTC-Th/Se) paired with P3CT-Na and Ag reproducibly push efficiency to ~18.5%, indicating effective passivation without disrupting charge extraction.

**Applying these rules to the pool:**

- **c097** (`ITCPTC-Se | C60 | BCP`, `P3CT-Na`, `Ag`) is a near-exact analog of the training champion combo `ITCPTC-Th | C60 | BCP / P3CT-Na / Ag` (18.49%) — just a chalcogen swap on the interfacial dye, expected to perform similarly well.
- **c044** (`PCBM-60 | BCP`, `PTAA`, `Cu`) directly matches the highest-performing PTAA+Cu recipe pattern (18.62–19.085% in training).
- **c088** (`C60 | BCP`, `PTAA`, `Cu`, Doctor blading) reproduces the exact ETL/HTL/contact combination of the two best training rows, differing only in coating method (doctor blading vs spin/slot-die), which should still give strong performance.
- **c085** (`TTC | C60 | BCP`, `PTAA`, `Ag`) matches the classic high-performing `C60 | BCP / PTAA / Ag` family (17.1–18.62%) with an added passivating interlayer (TTC), likely incremental improvement.
- **c034** (`PCBM-60 | C60 | BCP`, `PTAA`, `Al`) matches the fullerene-bilayer + PTAA architecture seen in several 14–19% entries; Al contact is slightly less optimal than Cu but still consistent with good performance.

## Final Answer

Final: c097, c044, c088, c085, c034
